Because the original message repeats itself a few times and uses some awkward phrasing (like "hand over back"), I have provided two options. 

**Option 1** is heavily polished to make it sound highly professional, clear, and easy to read. **Option 2** is closer to your original wording, just with the grammar fixed.

> "I am not sure if you still need the electronic copies of the documents I saved and typed for you prior to October 30, 2023, but I believe it is time to hand them over to you. 
>
> I have attached a picture of the black external hard drive so you know what it looks like. I will deliver it to you in person later. >

This means the black hard drive is the final item I will hand over to you containing your past documents. No other files, drives, or USB sticks will be handed over on my last day of work. 
>
> Please keep this hard drive in a safe place when I deliver it, as it contains confidential details, such as passwords. When you connect it to your computer, open the 'JWC' folder; inside, you will find a document called 'JWC Personal Book.xls.' This file contains the passwords you or your family members may need in the future. 
>
> Finally, the only physical items I still need to return to you or your family are: 
> 1. Two ATM bank cards (one for your personal HSBC account and one for the JWC-PC account)
> 2. One HSBC security device 
> 3. One Octopus card."

***

### Option 2: Minor Grammar Corrections (Closest to your original)
> "I am not sure if you still want to keep the electronic copies of the documents I saved and typed for you in the past (up to Oct 30, 2023), but I think it's time to hand them **over** to you. Attached is a picture of the black case to give you an idea of what it looks like, which I will deliver to you in person later. It has all the electronic copies of the documents I typed for you up to Oct 30, 2023. When you have time, you can connect the black case to your computer and take a look. 
>
> Starting Nov 1, 2023, I will send you the electronic copies of the documents (if any) you ask me to type via **email** only, and I will not save them on an external disk or USB stick for you in the future. This means the black case is the last item I will hand over to you that contains all the electronic copies of the documents you asked me to type or save in the past. No other files or external drives will be handed over on my last day of work. 
>
> Therefore, you need to keep the black case (**see attached photo**) in a safe place when I deliver it to you in person, as it contains confidential details such as passwords. If you connect the black case to your computer and look **in** the 'JWC' folder, you will see a document called 'JWC Personal Book.xls'. It contains the passwords I have for you that you or your family members may need in **the** future. 
>
> I think the only items that I **still need** to return to you or your family members are: 1) **Two** ATM bank cards (one is your personal HSBC account and the other is the JWC-PC account), 2) **One** HSBC security device for logging into your HSBC account, AND 3) **One** Octopus card."

### Key Corrections Made:
*   **"Hand over back to you"** -> Changed to "hand them over to you." The word "back" is redundant here.
*   **"Case"** -> It is much clearer to call this a "hard drive," "external drive," or "USB stick." Calling it a "black case" multiple times sounds a bit unnatural in English. 
*   **"EMAIL"** -> Changed to lowercase "email" (all-caps in emails looks like you are shouting).
*   **"External disk/case/USB stick"** -> Changed to "external drive or USB stick." Listing too many slash marks makes a sentence very hard to read.
*   **"Refer photo attached"** -> Changed to "see attached photo" for correct grammar. 
*   **"Return back"** -> Changed to "return." Saying "return back" is repetitive; "return" already means to give back. 
*   **Capitalization & Punctuation:** Fixed the capitalization of "HSBC" and transformed the items at the end into a clean numbered list so the recipient doesn't miss anything important.
